chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' Kirdeyn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The stoned man and the stoned woman are washed, embalmed, and enshrouded before that, then they are stoned, and Salat is prayed upon them; and the one killed in (legal) retaliation is at that status. He is washed, embalmed, enshrouded, and Salat is prayed upon him.

key_terms.الْمُقْتَصُّ: The one killed in legal retaliation (qisas)
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / equivalent to
key_terms.يُحَنَّطَانِ: They are embalmed (with musk and camphor)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for washing and praying funeral prayer on a person executed by stoning in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic status of those executed by stoning (rajm) or legal retaliation (qisas) as full-fledged Muslims entitled to burial rites, countering views that might exclude them. It establishes a specific ritual sequence: washing, embalming, and enshrouming occur prior to execution, followed by the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) after death, thereby affirming their spiritual dignity despite the punitive nature of their death. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity and communal prayer for the deceased, regardless of the cause of death.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Kirdeyn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The stoned man and the stoned woman should both be washed, and embalmed, and enshrouded before that, then they would be stoned, and Salaat would be prayed upon them; and the one killed in (legal) retaliation would be at that status. He would be washed, and embalmed, and enshrouded, and Salaat would be prayed upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma’ Kirdin who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Ghusl (bath), hunut, and shroud are done for people stoned to death, male or female, prior to executing stoning, then Salah (prayer) is performed. Ghusl (bath), hunut, shrouding and Salah (prayer) for one executed because of retaliation are also done before the execution.”’
